name: elevator-leg-dump
title: Elevator Leg Dump
description: An ambient loader modelled on a bucket elevator: a closed loop of 8 buckets climbs one straight, tips and empties into a chute as it crests the head pulley, then rides back down empty on the other side to be refilled at the boot — continuous circulation, never a percentage or a completion state.
useWhen: a background/batch process with no discrete percentage that needs an ambient 'still working' indicator rather than a generic spinner: pick elevator-leg-dump when continuous, cyclical throughput is the honest metaphor (nothing ever completes, buckets just keep circulating). Pick loader-thread-spool instead when total/loaded byte counts are actually known partway through the wait — that component explicitly converts an indeterminate coil into a real proportional gauge the instant a total arrives; this component has no such state and must never grow one, since a bucket elevator has no 0% or 100%, only circulation.
instruction: An ambient status loader shaped like a bucket elevator (a 'leg'): a stadium-shaped track (two vertical straights joined by two semicircular pulley caps) built from a single closed SVG `<path>` (stroke var(--border), the ~1.1:1 whisper-contrast separator token — structure, never the subject) plus two small hub circles at the head (top) and boot (bottom) pulley centers, also var(--border). Track geometry is derived every ResizeObserver tick from the container's smaller dimension: track height = 0.9 * min(w,h), track width = 0.35 * min(w,h), so it reads correctly at card scale. Eight bucket `<g>` elements share one continuous arc-length parametrisation of the stadium perimeter (a hand-written stadiumPoint(s) function returning position + direction-of-travel heading per straight/arc segment, not CSS offset-path, to keep the tip and fill events as simple pure functions of the same `s`); one full revolution takes a fixed real-time 8800ms, with the 8 buckets evenly spaced at perimeter/8 apart, so a bucket crests the head and dumps roughly every 1100ms. This is a deliberate decoupling from the real mechanic's rate (real chain speed 1.5-2.5 m/s, real bucket spacing 200-300mm, meaning a real fixed point sees 6-10 buckets/second) — animating that literally would alias against paint rate, so the documented real rate is only in this description, never rendered 1:1. Each bucket's own transform is `translate(x,y) rotate(heading + 90 + tipAngle)` recomputed every animation frame directly via setAttribute (no React state in the render loop; React state exists nowhere in the hot path). tipAngle is 0 everywhere except a ~520ms dump window centered on the head apex: it ramps from 0 to -100deg over the first 220ms (the bucket tipping as centrifugal force rounds the head pulley) then eases back to 0 over the following 300ms as the bucket starts down the descending leg, both computed as pure functions of the bucket's own arc-length position, not a timer or state machine. A `currentColor` streak line (color var(--foreground), never var(--ns-accent) — the dump moment is explicitly excluded from accent per the binding rules) fades in for the tip-down phase and fades out over a further 260ms, marking the dump. Each bucket also carries exactly one piece of persistent state: its current fill level, one of a fixed period-5 sequence (60%, 85%, 40%, 100%, 70%) that advances by one step the instant that specific bucket's own boot-crossing edge is detected (previous frame's time-since-boot negative, current frame's non-negative) — so the amount dumped visibly varies dump to dump, proving the loop is a real cycle and not decorative geometry. A bucket's visible content (an inner `<rect>` anchored to the cup floor, fill var(--foreground) for a real luminance step against both var(--background) and var(--border), never blended with var(--ns-muted) or var(--ns-accent)) is full while ascending, drains to 0 across the same 220ms tip-down window, stays empty across the entire descending leg, then rises back to its newly-assigned level over a 200ms fill window as the bucket starts back up from the boot — all as pure functions of arc-length position, so the whole system is stateless except the one fill-level value per bucket. At rest (t0/2.5s/5s, zero input): t0 shows all 8 buckets distributed around the track at their fixed 1100ms phase offsets, at least one mid-ascent and one mid-descent, all holding period-5 fill levels; by 2.5s roughly two dump events have occurred and every bucket has advanced ~28% around the loop; by 5s roughly 4-5 dumps have elapsed. `prefers-reduced-motion` computes geometry once, analytically derives the phase at which bucket 0 sits 180ms into its own dump window (named HEAD_CREST — one bucket mid-tip with its streak visible, the adjacent already-passed bucket upright and empty on the descending leg, and a bucket that has not yet reached the head fully upright and full on the ascending leg, so fill, transit and dump all read in one still frame), paints exactly that one frame via the same pure position functions, and never starts the rAF loop. An IntersectionObserver stops/resumes the rAF loop on visibility and a ResizeObserver (debounced 80ms) recomputes geometry and repaints on layout change; both, plus the rAF handle, are torn down on unmount. Every stroke/fill is a CSS custom property referenced directly in an SVG presentation attribute (var(--border), var(--foreground)) — there is no canvas, no GLSL and no JS colour computation anywhere, so there is nothing to read via getComputedStyle and nothing that could paint an unresolved colour before a token exists; the browser resolves the custom property natively on the very first paint. No pointer/press/scroll interaction of any kind (autoplay.mode is 'none'): this is a pure ambient status indicator, `role="status"` with a plain `aria-label` (default 'Working'), no `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuemax` and never a percentage anywhere in the DOM, matching the spec's explicit warning against adding a completion readout. Zero dependencies, DOM+SVG+CSS only.
